characters.continuity: Marvel Cinematic Universe films and Disney+ series, extended by Marvel Comics appearances including Marvel Comics Presents #72-84 (1991)
characters.summary: Logan during the Weapon X program: stripped of free will, mind-wiped, and forcefully bonded with liquid adamantium. In this feral, heavily augmented state, he operates as a lethal living weapon possessing retractable adamantium claws, an aggressive superhuman healing factor, and animalistic combat instincts before breaking out.

mechanisms: Indestructible adamantium skeleton and claw casing
Healing factor (wounds heal; shrugs off the drugs pumped into him)

weaknesses: Mental conditioning and psychological trauma from the Weapon X program
Vulnerability to psychological manipulation while in a feral state
His mind is wiped and controlled by the Weapon X staff through chemical and mechanical conditioning; for most of the story he is in a near-mindless state

Acts on conditioning and instinct rather than strategy while under Weapon X control
characters.formDifferences: Represents Logan specifically during his time as the mind-wiped, adamantium-bonded test subject of the Weapon X program, relying completely on feral instincts and newly fused claws rather than his later moral restraint.

sources.supports: General character background, adamantium bonding, and Weapon X history.
The Weapon X storyline details in Marvel Comics Presents #72-84.

Plot of Weapon X: the Professor, Cornelius and Hines wipe Logan's mind and bond adamantium to his bones to make a killing machine; adamantium-coated claws; he kills the soldiers at the wilderness site except Malcolm Colcord and escapes into the wilderness.

Weapon X (1991) details: he is forced to kill a pack of wolves and to fight and behead a grizzly bear; his wounds heal and he fights off the drugs; the mind control is chemical/mechanical; he goes into a frenzy, kills staff and escapes into the snow.
Review of Marvel Comics Presents #72-84: Logan was kidnapped and forced into the experiment; the adamantium infusion makes his claws pop out; he goes feral, stalking and killing doctors and soldiers.
